script: Why did Cristiano Ronaldo get FINED exactly ONLY €255 by Portugal? So the Portuguese Football Association just fined Cristiano Ronaldo €255 for the whole ordeal that went on a few weeks ago involving Coach Jorge Jesus and Ronaldo. By now, you probably already know the whole drama, but in short, Ronaldo was on the bench for Portugal's Nations League match against Norway, and Coach Jorge Jesus tells him to warm up for 30 minutes, then never puts him in. Then Ronaldo eventually packed his bags after a few more disrespectful moments and broken promises. Ronaldo eventually explained on social media everything that happened and even suggested that he, just like any other player, should be punished for leaving camp early. But that decision activated a rule most fans have never heard of. The Portuguese Football Federation charged him under Article 160 of their disciplinary code, which says any called-up player who abandons national team activity without justification gets a 1 to 6-month suspension, and if they're a professional, a fine between 5 and 10 units of account. One unit of account in Portuguese football equals exactly €102. So since the minimum punishment is 5 units, the minimum fine is €510. But Ronaldo didn't even get the minimum sentence. After walking out, he publicly apologized and said he'd accept any punishment, which triggered Article 244, which says if a player confesses without reservations, every penalty range gets cut in half. So his fine range dropped in half, and the federation gave him the absolute floor. So since the minimum was 5 units, which equals €510, that got halved because of Ronaldo's good behavior, and half of that is €255, which at Ronaldo's Al Nassr salary, he earns in about 38 seconds. So Portugal likely didn't want to give him a heavy punishment, so they don't add fuel to the fire.
